subject: Banking
title: How Mortgages Generate Billions
description: A micro-lesson that makes How Mortgages Generate Billions usable.

hook.text: US banks hold $12 trillion in mortgage debt. A 30-year mortgage at 7% pays the bank more in interest than the home.

buildup.text: A $400,000 mortgage at 7% over 30 years costs $558,000 in interest alone. The borrower pays nearly $1 million total.

discovery.text: Banks also charge origination fees of 0.5-1%. On a $400,000 loan, that's $2,000-$4,000 before a single payment is made.

twist.text: Banks often sell mortgages to investors and keep the servicing fee. They profit without holding the risk.

climax.text: Mortgages are the ultimate banking product. Long duration, secured by real property, and profitable at every stage.

punchline.text: $558,000 in interest on a $400,000 loan. Mortgages are profit machines.

quiz.question: How much interest does a $400,000 mortgage at 7% generate over 30 years?
